Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A

response.rationale: These are two separate concepts. A (ShipmentNotificationService, node 21902eaf2ee28c4a, src/notifications/application/shipment-notification.service.ts) is an application-layer service in the notifications component. It tells a customer that an order has shipped, as the quoted line shows: "await this.mailer.send(shipment.recipientEmail, 'Your order has shipped', `Shipped on ${day} with ${shipment.carrier}.`);". The service only reads shipment data (recipientEmail, carrier) to write an email. It does not model the shipment itself. B (Shipment, node e4b465cb4e5c3815, src/shipping/domain/shipment.ts, quoted line "export class Shipment {") is the domain entity for the physical shipment, in the shipping component. A notification about a shipment is a different real-world thing from the shipment. They share some data, but they are not one concept under two names.
